_comment: Chair-shaped NC bills whose operative text was READ AT SOURCE and matched against the ladder,
with each bill's full sponsor list. This is the campaign's working index: pull a bill's list ONCE,
then read it across the roster. Batch 04 produced 26 rows on four new source reads using this.
HOW TO USE: resolve each surname through nc-house-member-ids.json BY DISTRICT, never by name.
ncleg prints bare surnames with initials -- G./K./T. Brown are three different members, A. Jones
and B. Jones are two, R. Pierce and G. Pierce are two, F./N. Jackson are two.
BEFORE SEATING, CHECK conflicts_blank_these. A member on two bills pointing at adjacent chairs on
the same topic gets a BLANK, not the first chair you happened to find.
Sponsor lists were captured from BillLookUp via a summarising fetch. Treat them as a worklist:
re-confirm on the bill page before seating a member not already cross-checked.
PRIMARY SPONSORSHIP must be confirmed on the BILL page. A member's IntroducedBills page lists bills
they introduced, not only ones they primarily sponsored -- that error put a wrong sentence into a
live row for Alston and had to be corrected in prod.

🔴🔴 SPONSORSHIP: the /Sessions/ TEXT page's sponsor block is NOT reliable -- its 'primary sponsors' line silently includes cosponsors. BillLookUp is authoritative. This produced THREE wrong live rows (Alston/H1056, Garrett+Grafstein/S736, Alexander+Overcash/S724), each corrected in prod. Always read sponsorship from /BillLookUp/2025/<bill>.

bills.short_title: Equit. Escalation of Electricity Demand Act

bills.note: Deregulation PLUS $40M at 60-120% AMI in ONE bill. That pairing is why chair 3 fits and chair 4 does not.

bills.short_title: Equality in State Agencies/Prohibition on DEI
bills.note: Bans DEI programs AND race-based consideration in hiring, contracting and admissions, across state agencies, local government, UNC, community colleges and any body receiving public funds. Both clauses of chair 5. Contrast H799 (Echevarria, Setzer, Gable), which bars DEI funding but by its own terms does not reach voluntary initiatives or admissions -- that one seats NOTHING.
This ladder runs the OPPOSITE way: chair 1 = least oversight. Disclosure plus liability, no safety testing.
Pure deregulation, no money. Chair 4 only holds if the member has NO housing appropriation elsewhere.
ADU mandate, no money. Same caveat as H765 -- pairs with a subsidy bill into chair 3 instead.
Permitting incentives only. NOT a chair on its own; combines with a money bill to make chair 3.

bills.short_title: Fair Share for Public Schools Act
bills.note: 7% bracket above $1M into the State Public School Fund. States a RATE and a DESTINATION, which is what lets it clear the significantly-vs-moderately problem CLAUDE.md warns about.
PINS NOTHING. Section 1 creates deepfake liability; Section 2 grants developers immunity. Anyone whose only AI instrument is this bill gets a BLANK.

senate_bills.short_title: Foundation Act: Building NC's Housing Future
senate_bills.note: Has an INCLUSIONARY MANDATE (20% at 80% AMI), which is chair 2 language, but chair 2 also requires rent caps and this bill has none. All three of chair 3's clauses are met, so chair 3 -- understating beats asserting something false.

Funds AI AND regulates it: published safety protocol, annual independent audit, 72-hour incident reporting, penalties to 15% of training compute. Chair 4 needs a BAN on high-risk uses; the only prohibition is on what the FUND may support. Chair 3.

CRIMINAL (Class 3 misdemeanour on repeat) and requires NO shelter availability first -- that is chair 5. Contrast H781 at chair 4: civil-only and conditioned on documented shelter shortage. The mechanism, not the direction, picks the chair.
Deregulation, no money. Chair 4 ONLY for a member with no housing appropriation elsewhere; Mayfield has S446 so she is chair 3.
HELD. Halting a scheduled corporate cut is not raising a tax.
HELD. Restoring down-zoning authority is not named by any chair.
BLANK. Raises subsidy rates but states no eligibility band, so chairs 2 and 3 both partly fit.
BLANK. Halves parent copays within an income-tested program; same 2-vs-3 ambiguity.
BLANK. $25M/yr for FACILITY grants only -- meets chair 3's facility-grant clause but not its income-tested subsidy clause.
BLANK. Election-worker protection and audit rules; no chair names election administration.
BLANK. Automatic voter registration, but chair 1 also requires ONLINE VOTING. The ladder is compound at BOTH ends.
BLANK. Bans DEI offices/instruction in public education but never reaches hiring, contracting or admissions -- the same shortfall as H799. Contrast H171, which does and seats chair 5.
BLANK. Restroom and facility access, NOT sports eligibility.
BLANK. Lets students join sports at another school; nothing about transgender eligibility despite the title.
BLANK. 'Safe Camps Act' is about YOUTH CAMPS and campgrounds.
BLANK. 'Protecting Workers in the Age of AI Act' is a retraining fund plus layoff reporting; no AI duty at all.
